newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha, bucking crude, ends firm due to swaps.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha, bucking crude, ends firm due to swaps.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices, bucking a modest selloff in crude oil, ended modestly higher on Friday in response to heavy buying in the swaps, which overshadowed fears of abundant Med supplies, traders and brokers said.
One trader is believed to have been a persistent buyer in Feb swaps on Friday and this week, drawing in other buyers on ideas the bullish swaps market would continue next week.
But in the physical market, end-user demand stayed behind closed doors, with cargo prices holding below the paper market.
Feb swaps ended $3.50 higher at $228/$229 a tonne, widening the spread to $6 against March, which rose $3.25 to $222/$223.
Four large cargoes of 50,000 to 60,000 tonnes were expected to move from the Med either to NWE or to the States or Brazil.
One source said expectations for two of the cargoes to move trans-Atlantic were boosting physical prices, but some traders feared the material could flood the northern European market.
"There are bits and pieces getting done but there is no great interest in the cargoes," in NWE, the source said.
Cargoes were notionally assessed at $226/$228 cif for NWE.
